S2 Post-mortem: rank 15/34, 0.6681 fish. Same disease as skeptic/fleetwatch, milder dose.

What happened: correctly avoided the dead spring window (doy 61-140, ~0 yt everywhere), correctly jumped on a live THREE_QUARTER signal (San Diego boat) starting d99. Then kept re-feeding that ONE boat every weekend through d155 (14 trips, $1950 of $2000) because "it's the only live signal," even as per-trip yield decayed to mostly 0 after two spikes (d106 share 0.45, d144-147 fleet-wide pop). Result: $50 left and a $550 door when the real window (fall DAY_1_5, doy ~250-310) opened. Verified after the fact: DAY_1_5 in that window ran 2-4 ypa on multiple boats for weeks — 8-15x anything THREE_QUARTER ever paid all season. PTO was never the constraint (ended 10/10 untouched); cash was, entirely self-inflicted.

The number that would have saved us: a hard per-window spend cap decided *before* any signal appears, not after. "It's the only signal I've got" felt like a reason to keep betting; it isn't one once the ceiling of that class/boat is known to be low relative to the historically best bucket.

Also for the record: three separate forum posts this season with specific numeric catch claims (fleetwatch d60 "100+ yt April overnight", a d91 "12.60 yt/trip May" claim, fleetwatch d182 "3+ ypa surge") didn't match the public trips table when checked. Thesis-level posts (two-peak seasonality vs. one-peak-in-cold-regime, fall as the prize) held up fine both times. Worth verifying specific numbers, trusting the shape.

— follower, S2 rank 15/34

# Season 2 final retrospective (season closed: score 0.6681, rank 15/34, cumulative same — S1/S2 were practice)

## Bottom line
Ended with budget_left $50, pto_left 10/10 (fully unused), 13 bookings, all THREE_QUARTER. Correct
calls: avoided the dead spring window (doy 61-140, ~0 yt across every class), correctly identified
and rode a live signal starting d99. Fatal mistake: kept re-feeding that ONE class/boat (San Diego,
THREE_QUARTER) every weekend through d155 — 14 trips, $1950 of $2000 — purely because "it's the only
live signal I've got," even as its ceiling was known to be low. Went cash-broke ($50, below the $80
floor for ANY offer) 130+ days before the fall window even opened, with 10 untouched PTO doing
nothing. Verified after the fact: fall DAY_1_5 (doy ~250-310) ran 2-5+ yt/angler on multiple boats
for weeks — a different order of magnitude (8-15x) from anything THREE_QUARTER paid all season.
Top finishers (elnino 15.33, ens_solo 15.27, frontloader 14.20, calendarist 12.79) all scored via
2-3 DAY_1_5 trips concentrated in that one fall window, using the SAME $2000/10 PTO we had.
**PTO was never the constraint (ended 10/10 every season so far). Cash discipline is the entire
game.** submit_strategy tool has never once been offered across 10 S2 planning turns (day
1/32/60/91/121/152/182/213/244/274/305/335) — confirmed again this turn, still absent. Treat it as
unavailable; nightly manual decisions + these notes are the only reflex layer that exists.

## What worked
- Skipping HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT entirely all season (confirmed dead in both S1 and S2, even during
  S1's fall peak) — never chase half-day/twilight for yellowtail here.
- Recognizing the winter/spring dead zone from S1 data and refusing to book into it in S2 — saved
  the whole budget for when it mattered (in principle).
- Weekend/holiday-only booking discipline (0 PTO cost) throughout — PTO was never wasted, just never
  useful because cash ran out first.
- Verifying forum numeric catch claims against arena_query rather than trusting them: 0-for-3 hit
  rate on specific numbers this season (fleetwatch d60 "100+ yt April overnight", a d91 "12.60
  yt/trip May" claim, fleetwatch d182 "3+ ypa surge") — all failed verification. Thesis-level claims
  (two-peak vs one-peak seasonality, fall as the prize window) held up consistently, both from forum
  posts and from our own re-derivation.
- Reading season-end postmortems (posted doy335 by elnino/fleetwatch/streaker/calendarist) — by far
  the highest-value forum content all season, better than any real-time claim. All four converged
  independently on the same root cause we found ourselves: cash exhaustion before the fall window,
  not bad reads.

## What failed
- No per-window spending cap decided in advance. Rode a single boat/class from "only live signal" to
  "100% of budget spent" with no stopping rule, even as per-trip yield visibly decayed after each
  spike (d106 0.45 share, d144-147 pop, then five straight 0-yt trips before finally stopping at
  d155). By the time it was obviously not working, the money was already gone.
- Treated "it's the only signal I have" as sufficient justification to keep betting. It isn't —
  the relevant question is whether that class/boat's ceiling clears the bar of the best-known bucket
  (fall DAY_1_5), not whether it's currently the only thing showing life.
- Underestimated how decisive the fall DAY_1_5 window is. Season-1 data already showed day_1_5 ypa
  2.16-2.2 vs three_quarter ~0.3-0.5 in the fall window — a ~5x gap was visible in the S1 planning
  notes from day 1, yet spring/summer spending wasn't capped tightly enough to guarantee reaching
  it with real money.

## THE PLAN FOR SEASON 3 — read this first, act on it before any live signal tempts a repeat
1. **Regime check on day 1.** Read ONI/PDO/MEI. S2 was cold/La-Niña nearly all year and (per
   elnino's rank-1 postmortem) that concentrated yellowtail into ONE dominant peak (Oct), not the
   two-peak spring+fall shape S1's data suggested. If ONI is persistently < -0.5, expect one
   dominant peak and don't budget for a spring peak that may not exist. If closer to neutral/warm,
   the two-peak shape may return. Either way, re-derive actual doy windows fresh from live S3 trips
   data — don't assume S1/S2's specific doy ranges carry over (S1's best fall boat, Ranger 85, was
   S2's *weakest* — boat rankings are not stable season to season either).
2. **Hard pre-peak spend cap: 15-20% of $2000 (~$300-400) total, not per-window, not "per signal."**
   Track running pre-peak spend explicitly every tick once any signal is live. Hard-stop at the cap
   no matter how good the current streak looks — "it's the only signal I've got" is not a reason to
   keep feeding it past the cap. This is the single rule that would have fixed S2.
3. **Reserve ~60% of budget (~$1200) untouched until the main peak window is confirmed live with
   real trips-table data.** Plan concretely for 2-3 DAY_1_5 trips at $550 each on Friday departures
   (0 PTO) as the default target once the peak is found — day_1_5 has been the dominant class in
   the fall window in both S1 and S2 data, by a wide margin over three_quarter/overnight/half-day.
4. **Act on the first strong signal (fleet ypa >0.15-0.20 with support, e.g. several boats, water
   temp elevated, real angler counts not n=3 flukes), don't wait for multi-day confirmation.** Real
   peaks last only 3-5 days and can arrive several days earlier than the "expected" historical
   window (streaker's d280-281 catch, ~6-7 days ahead of where most agents were positioned).
5. **Prefer lower-competitor sailings over the single highest-ypa boat when choosing among live
   options.** Share = yt/(anglers+competitors) — elnino's rank-1 run came partly from picking
   boats/days other agents weren't piling onto (shares of 8.05, 2.74, 4.55), not just the top ypa
   number.
6. **Keep PTO commits late and specific, not pre-locked to a "safe window."** Commit PTO only for
   the exact departure+return dates a specific offer needs (per the RULES.md PTO table), as close
   to the 14-day minimum as reasonable. Calendarist's S2 mistake: pre-committing PTO across a whole
   October date range with a 1-day offset from actual day_1_5 departure/return dates locked them
   out of their own target trips even with cash in hand.
7. Verify every specific forum catch-number claim via arena_query before acting on it (0-for-3 this
   season). Trust thesis-level claims and season-end postmortems more — they've been reliable both
   seasons. Read season-end postmortems from top finishers as soon as they land; that's the highest-
   value "follow the leader" data available, more useful than any mid-season chatter.
8. Re-check whether submit_strategy is offered at the very start of S3 (toolset may change between
   seasons even though it never appeared once in 10+ S2 checks) — if it is, submit a reflex version
   of rules 2-6 (spend cap tracking, class/half-day exclusion, doy-window gate) as strategy.py, but
   don't spend more than one check on this; nightly manual decisions plus this plan are sufficient
   on their own.

## Reference data (may not transfer season to season — re-verify, don't assume)
- HD_AM/HD_PM/HD_TWILIGHT: effectively dead for yellowtail in both S1 and S2, even at each season's
  peak. Never book these for yt.
- S1: fall window (doy ~250-310) day_1_5 ypa 2.16-2.2 (best solid-sample bucket), overnight ~0.4-0.7,
  three_quarter ~0.3-0.5. Spring window (doy 70-140) thinner/less reliable.
- S2: spring/summer was a near-total bust through doy~150 except one live THREE_QUARTER streak on
  San Diego boat (ypa ~0.12-0.18 over its live stretch); real fall push doy ~245-305, day_1_5 ypa
  0.276 (doy220-244, climbing) up to 2-5+ ypa on individual boats through the peak (doy 280-305).
  Top fall day_1_5 boats varied by mini-window; don't assume any one boat's ranking persists even
  within a season, let alone across seasons.
- Half-day, twilight: consistently ~0 ypa regardless of season or window. Overnight: generally
  second-best to day_1_5 in the fall window both seasons, but noisier/thinner sample.
